---
name: factory-checkout-branch
description: Create a correctly named feature branch from the up-to-date base branch, carrying over any uncommitted work. Use when work was started on a shared branch (main, staging, develop…), or before starting a ticket.
argument-hint: "[ticket-or-description] [--base <branch>]"
---

<!-- Generated by sync-kit from factory-kit 0.10.0. Edit plugins/factory-kit in solo-factory, not this copy. -->

Create a feature branch for: `$ARGUMENTS`

1. **Where am I**: run `git status --porcelain`, `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`, and
   `git remote -v`. A **shared branch** is a long-lived branch others build on, never one to commit features to. It is any of:
   - the plugin's protected branches: `main,master,develop,staging` (default `main,master,develop,staging`);
   - `origin`'s default branch (`git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, strip `origin/`);
   - a branch the repo's `CLAUDE.md` names as the MR/PR target or says never to push to;
   - a branch CI deploys or verifies on push: `on.push.branches` in `.github/workflows/*.yml`, or
     the branch rules in `.gitlab-ci.yml`.
   If HEAD is not on a shared branch, it's already a feature branch: say so and stop. Otherwise
   continue, even if the shared branch isn't the base (work started on `staging` still moves to a
   feature branch cut from the base).
2. **Base branch**, first match wins:
   - `--base <branch>` in the arguments;
   - the MR/PR target branch named in the repo's `CLAUDE.md`;
   - `origin`'s default branch: `git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` (strip
     `origin/`). If none of these work, ask.
3. **Name**: `<type>/<ticket>-<slug>`.
   - `type` is a Conventional Commits type that fits the work: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `docs`,
     `test`, `chore`, `perf`.
   - `ticket` is the ticket id from the arguments (`T-123`, `#45`, `PROJ-9` → `t-123`, `45`,
     `proj-9`). Leave it out if there isn't one; never invent one.
   - `slug` is 2–5 lowercase words from the description or the uncommitted diff, joined by `-`.
   - If `CLAUDE.md` defines another branch naming convention, follow that instead.
   - If the name already exists locally or on origin, say so and ask for another.
4. **Create**:
   - `git fetch origin <base>`
   - `git switch --no-track -c <name> origin/<base>` (`git switch` keeps uncommitted changes in
     the working tree; `--no-track` stops the new branch from tracking `origin/<base>`, so a bare
     `git push` can't target the base). The first push sets its own upstream with `-u`. If git refuses because the changes conflict with `origin/<base>`, run
     `git switch -c <name>` from the current HEAD instead and tell the user the branch starts from
     their local base, which is behind origin.
   - No `origin` remote: skip the fetch and branch from the local `<base>` (`git switch -c <name>`
     while on it). Say the branch has no upstream yet.
   - Never `git reset`, `git checkout -- <file>`, `git stash drop`, or `git clean`. Uncommitted work
     must survive.
5. **Report**: the branch name, its base and base commit, and the uncommitted files that came along.
